sourceChecks.claim: Live PostgreSQL Concepts confirms managed relational data; previously inspected PostgreSQL backup documentation supports configured recovery and whole-database recovery obligations. Persistence alone is not all-failure protection.

Live PostgreSQL JSON Types confirms relational JSON capability; MongoDB transaction followup confirms configured multi-document transactions. Requirements must therefore assess actual product operations, not exclusive model categories.

Live MongoDB data-modeling document explains embedded documents, relationships and access-pattern-driven layout. PostgreSQL Concepts supplies rows/tables; direct known-key lookup is contrasted accurately with additional query structures.

Live Cassandra logical-modeling section explains query-first tables and partition/clustering keys; Neo4j primary followup confirms nodes/edges/traversal and pgvector confirms numeric distances and approximate speed/recall tradeoffs. Similarity is not a truth guarantee.

Live PostGIS documentation index followed to Getting Started confirms PostgreSQL extension/spatial SQL; pgvector primary README confirms PostgreSQL vector operations. Capability presence is distinct from workload equivalence.

Live PostgreSQL index introduction explains selective access and synchronization overhead. MongoDB modeling and Cassandra query-first layouts support duplication/read tradeoffs; distributed copies create communication and coordination obligations.

Live FoundationDB CAP page explains isolated replicas cannot see remote writes, and distinguishes CAP all-node availability from serving some clients; the lesson correctly scopes the conflict to partitions.

Live PostgreSQL Concepts plus inspected model/index/partition primary material supports the proposed requirements-first method. The final card gives evaluation advice, not an unsupported product-performance guarantee.
